facts.material: Laminated composite of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) film and polyethylene film, both plastics
facts.function: Packaging film providing barrier and structural protection
facts.form: Film, laminated, noncellular, not reinforced (roll or sheet form)
facts.end_use: Used as packaging material for products

gri_path: GRI 1: Heading 3920 covers 'other plates, sheets, film, foil and strip, of plastics, noncellular and not reinforced, laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials'; the PET/PE laminate is squarely described by this heading text
Chapter 39 note 1 confirms both PET and polyethylene are 'plastics'; note 2 exclusions do not apply
GRI 6: within 3920, PET film laminate falls under 3920.62 (poly(ethylene terephthalate)); no more specific 8/10-digit breakout applies so 'Other' (3920.62.00.90) governs

rejected_alternatives.reason: 3921 is a residual provision for reinforced/composite plastic sheets not covered elsewhere; heading 3920 explicitly and more specifically covers laminated plastic film combined with other plastic materials, which is the case here

missing_facts: Relative proportion/thickness of PET vs polyethylene (does not change heading but could affect classification if a non-plastic material were dominant)
Whether film is metallized or coated (would not change 3920.62 classification absent metal layer)
classification.rationale: Heading 3920 explicitly covers noncellular, non-reinforced plastic film laminated or combined with other materials, which precisely matches this PET-to-polyethylene laminate used for packaging. Chapter 39 Note 1 confirms both PET and polyethylene qualify as 'plastics,' and no chapter exclusion applies. Within 3920, the PET component controls classification to subheading 3920.62 (poly(ethylene terephthalate)), and absent a more specific breakout, the residual 'Other' statistical line 3920.62.00.90 applies, consistent with in-force rulings N338010 and N326371 classifying similar PET laminate films there. The 3921 argument is rejected because that heading is residual for reinforced/composite structures not otherwise provided for, whereas 3920's text directly and more specifically covers this laminated plastic film.

3920.argument: Heading 3920 covers 'Other plates, sheets, film, foil and strip, of plastics, noncellular and not reinforced, laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials.' The product is a laminated composite film consisting of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) laminated to polyethylene film. The heading text explicitly encompasses laminated plastic films combined with other materials. The product is in film form, used for packaging, and the PET component is the predominant plastic material. Subheading 3920.62 specifically covers PET films, and the 10-digit code 3920.62.00.90 ('Other') is the appropriate classification for PET film laminates not otherwise specified. Chapter 39 note 2 does not exclude this product—it is not a lubricant, wax, chemical compound, or any of the listed excluded articles. The product qualifies as a plastic article under Chapter 39 note 1 (capable of being formed under external influence and retained in shape). Multiple in-force CBP rulings (N338010, N326371) confirm that PET films, including laminated and coated variants, classify under 3920.62.

3921.argument: Heading 3921 covers 'Other plates, sheets, film, foil and strip, of plastics' and applies to reinforced, laminated, or composite plastic films. The product is a laminated composite of PET (polyethylene terephthalate) and polyethylene film used for packaging. While heading 3920 specifically covers 'noncellular and not reinforced, laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials,' the critical distinction is that 3920 applies when the plastic sheet itself is the primary component combined with other materials. However, when a laminated composite consists entirely of plastic layers (both PET and polyethylene are plastics), and the lamination creates a reinforced or composite structure that gives the material enhanced properties beyond a simple coated sheet, heading 3921 applies as the residual category for 'other' plastic sheets and films. The product's function as a packaging material with barrier and structural properties derived from the laminated composite structure supports classification under 3921 as a reinforced composite plastic film. Code 3921.90.15.00 applies to 'Other' composite plastic products not otherwise specified, with the notation '(229)' indicating products with non-textile reinforcement or composite construction.
exclusions_against: Heading 3920 explicitly covers 'noncellular and not reinforced, laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials,' which would apply if the product were a simple laminate of PET to polyethylene without reinforcement. Multiple CROSS rulings (N331595, N338010, N351059, N326371) classify similar PET-based laminated films under heading 3920.62 when the lamination is to polyethylene or involves coating/metallizing of a PET substrate, suggesting 3920 may be the more specific provision for this type of composite.

gri_path: GRI 1: Heading 3918 specifically names 'floor coverings of plastics, whether or not self-adhesive, in rolls or in the form of tiles', matching the product exactly; no Chapter 39 exclusion applies
GRI 6: Subheading 3918.10 (of polymers of vinyl chloride) applies given PVC material; within it, 'Vinyl tile' at 3918.10.10 matches form
GRI 6 (10-digit): Absent evidence of a rigid solid or rigid expanded polymer core, the residual 'Other' statistical line 3918.10.10.40 applies

rejected_alternatives.reason: 3918 is a more specific eo nomine provision for plastic floor coverings in tile form; 3926 is a residual basket heading
3920 covers unfinished plastic plates/sheets; the product is a finished floor covering tile specifically named in 3918

missing_facts: Whether the tile core is a rigid solid polymer core or rigid expanded polymer core (would change 10-digit suffix to .10.20 or .10.30 instead of .10.40)
classification.rationale: Heading 3918 expressly covers floor coverings of plastics in tile form, and PVC vinyl tiles fall squarely within subheading 3918.10 (of polymers of vinyl chloride), specifically 'Vinyl tile.' No chapter or section note excludes this product, and in-force rulings N327606 and N261168 confirm PVC vinyl tiles are classified here. Absent facts establishing a rigid solid or rigid expanded polymer core construction, the residual statistical suffix 'Other' (3918.10.10.40) is used as the default, though this could change with additional construction details.

3918.argument: Heading 3918 explicitly covers 'Floor coverings of plastics, whether or not self-adhesive, in rolls or in the form of tiles.' The product is PVC vinyl tiles, which are plastic floor coverings in tile form. Subheading 3918.10 applies to floor coverings 'of polymers of vinyl chloride,' which directly matches the material composition. The product falls under 3918.10.10 (Vinyl tile), and the 10-digit code 3918.10.10.40 (Other) is the appropriate classification for vinyl tiles that do not consist of a rigid solid polymer core or a rigid expanded polymer core as specified in the more specific 10-digit lines. Chapter 39 note 2 does not exclude floor coverings from chapter 39, and Section VII note 2 specifically carves out an exception for headings 3918 and 3919 regarding printed articles, confirming that 3918 is the proper home for plastic floor coverings. Multiple in-force CBP rulings (N327606, N261168, N034816) confirm that PVC vinyl tiles are classified in 3918.10.10.xx, with the specific 10-digit suffix depending on the tile's construction.

3926.argument: Heading 3926 covers 'Other articles of plastics and articles of other materials of headings 3901 to 3914.' PVC vinyl tiles are plastic articles made from polyvinyl chloride, a plastic material. The tiles are formed by molding or extrusion under heat and pressure, meeting the definition of plastics in Chapter 39 Note 1. As plastic articles not specifically provided for in other headings, they fall within the residual scope of heading 3926.
exclusions_against: Heading 3918 explicitly covers 'Floor coverings of plastics, whether or not self-adhesive, in rolls or in the form of tiles.' This is a more specific heading that directly describes the product. Chapter 39 Note 2(o) excludes wall coverings of heading 4814 from Chapter 39, but does not exclude floor coverings of heading 3918. Heading 3918 is the proper classification for PVC vinyl tiles used as floor coverings.

3920.argument: Heading 3920 covers 'Other plates, sheets, film, foil and strip, of plastics, noncellular and not reinforced, laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials.' PVC vinyl tiles in their basic form—as plastic sheets or plates—fall within this heading's scope as plastic articles not specifically excluded. The material is polyvinyl chloride (PVC), a plastic polymer covered by Chapter 39. The tiles are plastic plates or sheets in their primary manufactured form before installation.
exclusions_against: Heading 3918 'Floor coverings of plastics, whether or not self-adhesive, in rolls or in the form of tiles' is more specific and directly describes PVC vinyl tiles in tile form intended for flooring. Chapter 39 note 2(o) excludes wall coverings of heading 4814 but does not exclude floor coverings. The CROSS rulings N327606, N261168, N341739, N034816, and F88852 all classify PVC vinyl tiles under heading 3918.10 (vinyl chloride floor coverings), not 3920. Heading 3918 is the specialized provision for finished floor coverings in tile form, making it more specific than the general 3920 provision for plastic plates and sheets.

facts.form: Complete knitted garment, rib knit crew neckline, short hemmed sleeves, straight hemmed bottom

gri_path: GRI 1: Heading 6109 specifically names 'T-shirts...knitted or crocheted', a more specific description than the general 'shirts' heading 6105
Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms coverage of made-up knitted articles; no exclusion applies since bottom is straight-hemmed, not a tightening waistband

Section XI Note 2(A): for a 50/50 cotton/man-made fiber blend with no single fiber predominating by weight, the good is classified under the heading/subheading that occurs last in numerical order among those equally meriting consideration
GRI 6: comparing 6109.10 (of cotton) and 6109.90 (of man-made fibers) at the same subheading level, 6109.90 is last in numerical order and controls the 50/50 blend

rejected_alternatives.reason: Heading 6105 covers shirts generally; heading 6109 more specifically names T-shirts, singlets and similar garments, which better describes this jersey knit crew-neck garment
Cotton does not predominate by weight in an equal 50/50 blend; Section XI Note 2(A) directs classification to the heading last in numerical order among equally specific options, i.e., 6109.90

classification.rationale: Heading 6109 specifically names T-shirts knitted or crocheted, making it more specific than the general shirt heading 6105 under GRI 1/3(a); Chapter 61 Note 5's exclusion for tightening features at the bottom does not apply because the garment has a straight hemmed bottom. Because the fabric is an even 50/50 cotton-polyester blend with neither fiber predominating, Section XI Note 2(A) directs classification to the subheading occurring last in numerical order among those equally specific, which is 6109.90 (of man-made fibers) rather than 6109.10 (of cotton). The 10-digit statistical suffix for boys' T-shirts of man-made fibers is 6109.90.10.09, consistent with in-force rulings G88092 and M84378 addressing similarly constructed boys' knit T-shirts.

6109.argument: Heading 6109 covers T-shirts, singlets, tank tops and similar garments, knitted or crocheted. The product is a boys' T-shirt made of finely knit jersey fabric with a rib knit crew neckline, short hemmed sleeves, and a straight hemmed bottom—all characteristics that match the heading description. Chapter 61 note 1 confirms this chapter applies only to made up knitted or crocheted articles, which this garment is. Chapter 61 note 5 states that heading 6109 does not cover garments with a drawstring, ribbed waistband or other means of tightening at the bottom; this garment has a straight hemmed bottom, so it does not fall within that exclusion. The material is 50% cotton and 50% polyester. Under GRI 2(b), a reference to a material includes goods consisting wholly or partly of such material. Under GRI 3(b), composite goods are classified according to the material or component giving them essential character. Cotton and polyester are equally weighted (50/50), but the garment is not controlled by a single material. However, the 6-digit subheading 6109.10 (Of cotton) applies when cotton is the predominant material or gives essential character. Since the blend is equal, the garment falls under 6109.90 (Of other textile materials), specifically 6109.90.10 (Of man-made fibers), because polyester is a man-made fiber and the blend includes it. The best 10-digit code is 6109.90.10.09 (Boys'), which matches the product's end use as boys' casual wear. Supporting rulings G88092 and M84378 classify boys' T-shirts of similar construction (finely knit jersey, rib knit crew neckline, short hemmed sleeves, straight hemmed bottom) under heading 6109, confirming the classification approach.
exclusions_against: Chapter 61 note 5 excludes garments with a drawstring, ribbed waistband or other means of tightening at the bottom of the garment; this product has a straight hemmed bottom, so it does not trigger this exclusion

6105.argument: Heading 6105 covers 'Men's or boys' shirts, knitted or crocheted.' The product is a complete boys' T-shirt made of knitted jersey fabric with a crew neckline, short sleeves, and hemmed bottom—all hallmarks of a shirt under this heading. Chapter 61 note 1 confirms this chapter applies only to made-up knitted articles, which this product is. Chapter 61 note 4 specifies that heading 6105 does not cover sleeveless garments or garments with pockets below the waist, ribbed waistbands, or fewer than 10 stitches per linear centimeter; the product has short sleeves and finely knit jersey (meeting the stitch requirement), so it qualifies. The 50/50 cotton-polyester blend is a composite textile. Under GRI 2(b), a reference to a material includes mixtures of that material with others. The product is classifiable under 6105.10 (of cotton) because cotton comprises 50% by weight. The best 10-digit code is 6105.10.00.30 (Other boys' shirts of cotton), which is the residual category for boys' cotton knit shirts not imported as parts of playsuits.
exclusions_against: Chapter 61 note 4 excludes sleeveless garments from heading 6105, but this product has short sleeves, so the exclusion does not apply.

facts.material: Metal and plastic components (valve, housing, tubing, regulator)
facts.function: Dispenses bottled beer by controlling flow using hand-operated valve and compressed CO2 pressure
facts.form: Complete assembled home appliance with integrated valve, regulator, and dispensing mechanism

gri_path: GRI 1: Heading 8210 specifically names 'hand-operated mechanical appliances...used in the...serving of food or drink', which matches this dispenser precisely
Chapter 82 Note 1 carve-out: heading 8210 is expressly exempted from the working-edge/blade requirement that otherwise limits chapter 82
GRI 6: single statistical line 8210.00.00.00, no further subheading breakout

rejected_alternatives.reason: 8481 covers taps/valves as such; heading 8210 more specifically describes the complete hand-operated appliance used for serving drink, making 8210 the more specific and on-point heading under GRI 1/3(a)
Chapter 39 note 2(s) excludes articles that are more specifically covered as mechanical appliances of Section XV/XVI; 8210's specific language for drink-serving appliances controls

missing_facts: Confirm total assembled weight is 10 kg or less to satisfy heading 8210's weight limit
classification.rationale: Heading 8210 expressly and specifically covers 'hand-operated mechanical appliances, weighing 10 kg or less, used in the...serving of food or drink,' which is an exact match for a hand-operated beer dispensing valve appliance. Chapter 82 Note 1 explicitly carves out heading 8210 from the general requirement that chapter 82 articles have a blade or working edge, so the lack of a cutting component does not exclude it. This heading is more specific than the general valve provision of 8481 or the residual plastics household-articles heading 3924, satisfying GRI 3(a) even before reaching GRI 3(b). In-force ruling R01157 supports classifying a comparable drink dispenser under this same 10-digit line.

8481.argument: Heading 8481 covers 'Taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances, for pipes, boiler shells, tanks, vats or the like, including pressure-reducing valves and thermostatically controlled valves; parts thereof.' The home beer dispenser is a complete assembled appliance with an integrated hand-operated valve that controls the flow of bottled beer using compressed CO2 pressure. The valve mechanism is the essential functional component that defines the article. The product falls within 8481.80 (Other appliances) as a hand-operated valve appliance. Under GRI 6, subheading 8481.80.50 applies to hand-operated appliances of other materials (metal and plastic components). The 10-digit code 8481.80.50.90 (Other) is the appropriate statistical line for a home beer dispenser that does not fit the specific categories of pressure spray can valves or bath/shower/sink faucets.
exclusions_against: Chapter 84 note 1(f) excludes 'Electromechanical domestic appliances of heading 8509' but this product is hand-operated, not electromechanical, so the exclusion does not apply.
Section XVI note 1 does not contain exclusions that would remove valve appliances from Chapter 84 coverage.

8210.argument: Heading 8210 covers 'Hand-operated mechanical appliances, weighing 10 kg or less, used in the preparation, conditioning or serving of food or drink, and base metal parts thereof.' The beer dispenser is a hand-operated mechanical appliance (controlled by a hand-operated valve) designed specifically for serving beverages (beer). It is complete and assembled, weighs under 10 kg, and consists of metal and plastic components. The product directly fits the statutory language of heading 8210 as an appliance used in the serving of drink. Ruling R01157 (in force, 2004) classified a drink dispenser under 8210.00.0000 on identical reasoning. The product is not excluded by Chapter 82 notes, which apply only to articles with blades, working edges, or cutting surfaces—none of which this dispenser possesses.
exclusions_against: Chapter 82 Note 1 excludes articles without a blade, working edge, working surface or other working part of base metal, metal carbides, or abrasive materials—but this exclusion does not apply to heading 8210, which is carved out as an exception ('apart from...goods of heading 8209, this chapter covers only...')

3924.argument: Heading 3924 covers 'Tableware, kitchenware, other household articles and hygienic or toilet articles, of plastics.' A home beer dispenser is a household article made of plastic and metal components designed for home beverage service. The product functions as a dispensing appliance for domestic use, similar to other household beverage service items. Chapter 39 note 2(s) excludes 'Articles of section XVI (machines and mechanical or electrical appliances),' but this product is hand-operated and not primarily a machine or mechanical appliance in the sense of Chapter 84 machinery. The dispenser is fundamentally a household article for serving beverages at home, making it classifiable under heading 3924 as 'other household articles' of plastics rather than as industrial machinery.
exclusions_against: Chapter 39 note 2(s) excludes articles of Section XVI (machinery and mechanical appliances); a hand-operated valve-based dispenser with CO2 regulator may be argued to fall within heading 8481 (taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances) as demonstrated by ruling H250151 classifying a similar wine dispenser in 8481.80.50
Chapter 39 note 2(m) excludes containers of heading 4202, but this is an integrated dispenser, not a container

Revoked rulings N016275 and L89010 previously classified similar plastic dispensers with hand-operated valves in 3926.90 (other articles of plastics), suggesting the product may not fit squarely in 3924 tableware/kitchenware subcategories

facts.function: Rapid equalization of tank pressure and downstream line pressure
facts.form: Complete internal valve unit with multiple actuation modes (manual, air, cable)
facts.end_use: Pressure regulation/control in tank and pipeline fluid systems

gri_path: GRI 1: Heading 8481 expressly covers 'taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances, for pipes, boiler shells, tanks, vats or the like'; Section XVI Note 1 and Chapter 84 Note 1 exclusions do not apply
GRI 6: Within 8481, the valve is not a pressure-reducing valve (8481.10), transmission valve (8481.20), check valve (8481.30) or safety/relief valve (8481.40); it falls to 8481.80 'Other appliances'
GRI 6: Within 8481.80.90, the valve's non-specific actuation types (manual/air/cable) place it in the residual 'Other' statistical line 8481.80.90.50

rejected_alternatives.reason: Not specifically a pressure-reducing valve
Not a check valve
Not a safety or relief valve
Product is a complete valve, not a part

missing_facts: Exact material composition of valve body
Precise mechanism classification if it matches a more specific 8481.80 subcategory
classification.rationale: Heading 8481 explicitly names valves for tanks and pipes including pressure control functions, matching the product's described purpose. No section or chapter exclusion removes it, and it is a complete appliance rather than a part, so it is classified under the main heading. Because it does not meet the specific descriptions for pressure-reducing, transmission, check, or safety/relief valves, it falls to the residual 'other appliances, other, other' line 8481.80.90.50, consistent with in-force rulings I89615 and I85352 on similar multi-actuation industrial valves.

8481.argument: Heading 8481 covers 'Taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances, for pipes, boiler shells, tanks, vats or the like, including pressure-reducing valves and thermostatically controlled valves; parts thereof.' The product is an internal valve designed for rapid equalization of tank pressure and downstream line pressure, which is a core function of valves covered by this heading. The valve can be operated manually, by air, or by cable, incorporating various valve mechanisms. This multi-mode operation and pressure equalization function place it squarely within heading 8481's scope. The product is a complete valve unit (not a part), so it classifies under the main heading rather than 8481.90 (parts). Within 8481.80 (Other appliances), the valve does not fit the specific categories of pressure-reducing valves (8481.10), oleohydraulic/pneumatic transmission valves (8481.20), or check valves (8481.30), nor is it a safety/relief valve (8481.40). Under 8481.80.90 (Other appliances not otherwise specified), the valve's multi-mode actuation (manual, air, cable) and pressure equalization function best fit 8481.80.90.50 (Other), which captures valves with non-standard actuation mechanisms not covered by the more specific subcategories (solenoid, ballcock, regulator, control valves with hydraulic or thermostatic actuators). Chapter 84 note 1 does not exclude valves, and Section XVI note 1 does not exclude this product. The product is not a part or accessory but a complete appliance suitable for use in industrial fluid systems.

facts.material: Blend of cotton, nylon (man-made fiber), and metallic yarn
facts.function: Worn as an upper body garment for warmth and style
facts.form: Knitted or crocheted sweater, complete and finished

gri_path: GRI 1: Heading 6110 covers sweaters, pullovers and similar articles, knitted or crocheted; Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms coverage
Section XI Note 2(A): mixed fiber goods classified as if wholly of the predominating textile material by weight
GRI 6: comparison of subheadings 6110.20 (cotton), 6110.30 (man-made fibers), 6110.90 (other) at the same level

rejected_alternatives.reason: Would apply only if cotton is shown to predominate by weight over man-made fibers per Section XI Note 2(A); not established on these facts
Would apply if metallic/other fibers predominate by weight; ruling M85371 shows this outcome is possible with different blend ratios, but not confirmed here
No indication of 23%+ wool, 30%+ silk, or 25%+ leather content

missing_facts: Exact percentage by weight of cotton vs. nylon vs. metallic yarn is required to apply Section XI Note 2(A) and confirm which subheading (6110.20 cotton, 6110.30 man-made fiber, or 6110.90 other) governs
Confirmation that wool/fine animal hair, silk, or leather content thresholds are not met (assumed not met absent contrary facts)
classification.rationale: Heading 6110 clearly covers this knitted women's sweater under GRI 1, but the correct 6-digit subheading turns on which fiber predominates by weight under Section XI Note 2(A), and the description does not state percentages. Cited rulings show that similar cotton/nylon/metallic blends have been classified variously under 6110.30 or 6110.90 depending on actual composition, so a specific 10-digit code cannot be confirmed without the weight breakdown. The best-guess code 6110.30.30.20 assumes man-made fiber (nylon) predominates and that wool/silk/leather thresholds are not met, consistent with the closer-fact ruling K85028.

6110.argument: Heading 6110 covers sweaters, pullovers, sweatshirts and similar articles, knitted or crocheted. The product is a complete, finished women's sweater made from a blend of cotton, nylon (man-made fiber), and metallic yarn. Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms this chapter applies only to made up knitted or crocheted articles, which this sweater is. Section XI Note 2(A) provides that goods of mixed textile materials are classified as if consisting wholly of the textile material that predominates by weight. The product contains cotton, nylon, and metallic yarn in a blend; without specific weight percentages stated, the classification depends on which material predominates. Under GRI 6, the subheading is determined by comparing subheadings at the same level. Subheading 6110.20 covers sweaters of cotton; 6110.30 covers sweaters of man-made fibers; and 6110.90 covers sweaters of other textile materials. Since the product is a blend without a single predominating material clearly identified, and given that nylon (a man-made fiber) is explicitly named as a component, 6110.30 (Of man-made fibers) is the appropriate subheading. Within 6110.30, the product does not contain 25% or more leather (6110.30.10), 23% or more wool (6110.30.15), or 30% or more silk (6110.30.20), so it falls under 6110.30.30 (Other). This classification is supported by ruling M85371 (in force), which classified a women's sweater with 95.6% acrylic, 2.4% nylon and 2% metallic yarn under 6110.90.9030, and ruling K85028 (in force), which classified a woman's knitted sweater with 47.5% acrylic, 17.4% cotton, 15.3% wool, 11.8% nylon, 5.3% polyester and 2.7% mylar under 6110.30.3020. Both rulings confirm that multi-fiber blends containing nylon and metallic components are classified under heading 6110. The product meets all requirements: it is a made-up, knitted or crocheted article designed to cover the upper body, and contains man-made fibers (nylon) as a significant component.
exclusions_against: Section XI Note 1 excludes certain materials (animal hair, asbestos, etc.) but none apply to this cotton-nylon-metallic blend. Chapter 61 Note 2 excludes worn clothing and orthopedic appliances, neither of which applies. No exclusions prevent classification in heading 6110.

facts.function: Regulates fuel pressure and flow for gaseous-fueled engines
facts.end_use: Component for gaseous-fueled internal combustion engines (natural gas or LP gas)

gri_path: GRI 1: Heading 8481 names 'taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances... including pressure-reducing valves' which describes a self-operating fuel regulator as a good in its own right

Section XVI Note 2(a): parts which are goods included in a heading of chapter 84 (such as valves of 8481) are classified in their own heading rather than as parts of the engine, so heading 8409 is displaced
GRI 6: within 8481.80.90, 'Regulator valves, self-operating, for controlling variables such as temperature, pressure, flow and liquid level' matches the product

rejected_alternatives.reason: Section XVI Note 2(a) requires a part which is itself a good named in a chapter 84 heading (a valve/regulator of 8481) to be classified there, not as an engine part under 8409
Heading 8407 covers engines themselves, not regulator components; heading text does not extend to parts or accessories

missing_facts: Whether the regulator is a standalone component or integrated into a larger assembly
Whether it is a simple pressure-reducing valve or incorporates additional electronic/mechanical control functions that could implicate a different heading
classification.rationale: A fuel regulator for gaseous-fueled engines functions as a self-operating pressure-reducing/regulating valve, squarely within the heading 8481 text covering 'taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances... including pressure-reducing valves.' Section XVI Note 2(a) mandates that parts which are themselves goods described by a heading of chapter 84 (such as valves) be classified under that heading rather than as engine parts under 8409, so the 8409 argument fails despite being facially plausible. Heading 8407 is rejected because it covers only engines, not components. In-force rulings H262289 and N358644 support classifying gas fuel-system regulator/valve components under heading 8481, and GRI 6 places the article in the specific statistical line 8481.80.90.15 for self-operating regulator valves.

8481.argument: A fuel regulator for gaseous-fueled engines is a valve-type appliance that regulates fuel pressure and flow. Heading 8481 covers 'Taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances, for pipes, boiler shells, tanks, vats or the like, including pressure-reducing valves and thermostatically controlled valves.' A fuel regulator is a self-operating regulator valve that controls pressure—a core function within the scope of heading 8481. The product is a complete, functional assembly (not a part), made of metal, designed to regulate gaseous fuel delivery to internal combustion engines. Chapter 84 notes do not exclude it. The best 10-digit code is 8481.80.90.15 ('Regulator valves, self-operating, for controlling variables such as temperature, pressure, flow and liquid level'), which directly describes a self-operating pressure regulator. Ruling H262289 (in force) examined a compressed natural gas fuel tank system and confirmed that a high-pressure regulator reducing gas pressure for engine delivery falls within heading 8481. Ruling N358644 (in force) classified a fuel injector under 8481.80.9050, confirming that fuel system components for engines are properly classified in heading 8481.

8409.argument: A fuel regulator for gaseous-fueled engines is a part suitable for use solely or principally with internal combustion piston engines of heading 8407 or 8408. Heading 8409 covers 'Parts suitable for use solely or principally with the engines of heading 8407 or 8408.' The fuel regulator regulates fuel pressure and flow, making it an essential component part of gaseous-fueled engine systems. Since the regulator is designed for gaseous-fueled engines (natural gas or LP gas), it does not fall under subheading 8409.91, which is limited to spark-ignition engines. Instead, it classifies under 8409.99 'Other' parts for compression-ignition or other engine types. The best 10-digit code is 8409.99.99.00 for other parts not otherwise specified, as the regulator is a complete assembly suitable for use with gaseous-fueled engines but not specifically enumerated in the tariff schedule.
exclusions_against: Chapter 84 note 1 does not exclude engine parts from chapter 84; Section XVI note 1 does not exclude this part; the regulator is not a transmission, conveyor belt, or other excluded article

8407.argument: A fuel regulator for gaseous-fueled engines is a part suitable for use solely or principally with spark-ignition or compression-ignition internal combustion piston engines. Heading 8407 covers spark-ignition reciprocating or rotary internal combustion piston engines, and heading 8409 covers parts suitable for use solely or principally with the engines of heading 8407 or 8408. However, the user requests classification under heading 8407 itself. A fuel regulator is a component that regulates fuel pressure and flow—it is not itself an engine. Under GRI 1, a fuel regulator does not meet the description of heading 8407, which names 'engines.' The regulator is a part or accessory of an engine, not an engine. Heading 8409 is the proper heading for parts suitable for use solely or principally with engines of heading 8407 or 8408. For gaseous-fueled engines (natural gas or LP gas), the best code under 8409 would be 8409.99.99 (Other parts for other engines). However, if the regulator is for a spark-ignition gaseous engine, 8409.91.99 would apply. Since the product description specifies 'gaseous-fueled engines' without limiting to spark-ignition only, 8409.99.99 is the most appropriate. Nevertheless, arguing for heading 8407 as requested: a fuel regulator could theoretically be viewed as an incomplete or unfinished component that has the essential character of a gaseous-fueled engine under GRI 2(a), but this is a weak argument because a regulator alone does not constitute an engine or have the essential character of one. The regulator is a control component, not the prime mover. Heading 8407 text does not include regulators; they are accessories. The argument for 8407 fails under GRI 1 because the heading text does not cover parts or accessories—only engines themselves.
exclusions_against: Heading 8407 covers only 'Spark-ignition reciprocating or rotary internal combustion piston engines'—the text does not include parts, accessories, or regulators. A fuel regulator is not an engine.
Chapter 84 Note 1 does not exclude parts from chapter 84, but GRI 1 requires that the heading text itself must cover the article. Heading 8407 text is limited to engines, not their parts.
Section XVI Note 1 does not exclude parts and accessories of machinery from section XVI, but heading 8407 specifically names only engines, not their components.

facts.function: Controls fluid flow and pressure within an automatic transmission's hydraulic control valve assembly
facts.form: Spool valve part, a component of a larger valve body/assembly (not a complete valve)
facts.end_use: Installed in automatic transmissions of motor vehicles to regulate hydraulic fluid flow

gri_path: GRI 1: Heading 8481 covers 'taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances... parts thereof'; a spool valve part is specifically a part of a valve

Section XVII Note 2(e) excludes machines and appliances of heading 8481 (valves) and their parts from classification as 'parts' of motor vehicles under 8708, even though the valve is used in a vehicle transmission
GRI 6: Within 8481, subheading 8481.90 covers parts; 8481.90.90.85 is the residual 'Other' statistical line for parts not more specifically described

rejected_alternatives.reason: Section XVII Note 2(e) excludes articles of heading 8481 (valves and parts thereof) from the parts provisions of chapter 87, even when used in motor vehicle transmissions

Heading 8483 covers transmission shafts, gears, gear boxes and similar mechanical transmission elements; a spool valve is a fluid-control valve component, not a toothed/mechanical transmission element, and prior rulings classify similar valve bodies under 8481 rather than 8483

missing_facts: Whether the item is a complete valve assembly or only an internal spool component of a valve body (affects whether it is classified as a valve or merely a part of a valve)
Precise metal composition (ferrous vs. non-ferrous) though this does not change the 6-digit/8-digit classification here
Whether the part is designed solely/principally for one specific transmission model (relevant only for potential USTR/301 or other secondary considerations)
classification.rationale: A transmission spool valve part functions as a component of a fluid-control valve assembly, squarely within heading 8481's coverage of valves and parts thereof; Section XVII Note 2(e) excludes such valve parts from classification under heading 8708 as motor vehicle parts, notwithstanding their use in an automatic transmission. Because the article is described as a 'part' rather than a complete valve, and no more specific parts provision within 8481.90 applies, it falls to the residual statistical line 8481.90.90.85. In-force rulings N348390, N268111, and 963031 support classifying analogous transmission valve components under heading 8481 rather than 8483 or 8708, though exact match to this specific spool geometry was not independently verified.

8708.argument: A transmission spool valve part is a component of an automatic transmission hydraulic control system used in motor vehicles. Heading 8708 covers 'Parts and accessories of the motor vehicles of headings 8701 to 8705.' The spool valve is a specialized part designed solely for use in automatic transmissions to control fluid flow and pressure. It falls under 8708.40 (Gear boxes and parts thereof) as a transmission control component, or more broadly under 8708.99 (Other parts and accessories). Within 8708.99, the part qualifies as 'Other parts for power trains' under 8708.99.68 or as 'Other' under 8708.99.81. Since a spool valve is a precision-machined metal component that does not fit the specific categories listed (brake hoses, wheel hub units, slide-in campers, cable traction devices), it falls under 8708.99.81.80 (Other). Section XVII note 2 does not exclude this part as a 'part of general use'—it is a specialized transmission control component. Chapter 87 note 1 does not apply (not railway stock). The part is solely or principally used as a component of automatic transmissions for motor vehicles, satisfying the requirement for parts classification under Section XVII.
exclusions_against: Section XVII note 2(b) excludes 'parts of general use' of base metal, but a transmission spool valve is a specialized component, not a part of general use

8481.argument: Heading 8481 covers 'Taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances, for pipes, boiler shells, tanks, vats or the like, including pressure-reducing valves and thermostatically controlled valves; parts thereof.' A transmission spool valve part is a component of a valve assembly used to control fluid flow and pressure in an automatic transmission hydraulic system. The part falls squarely within the scope of heading 8481 as a part of a valve appliance. Subheading 8481.90 provides for 'Parts' of such valves. The 10-digit code 8481.90.90.85 classifies other parts not specifically enumerated, which is appropriate for a spool valve component. Chapter 84 note 1 does not exclude valve parts, and Section XVI note 1 does not exclude transmission control components. The product is a mechanical part of a valve system, not a transmission belt, leather article, or other excluded item.

8483.argument: A transmission spool valve part is a component of an automatic transmission control system. Heading 8483 covers 'Transmission shafts (including camshafts and crankshafts) and cranks; bearing housings, housed bearings and plain shaft bearings; gears and gearing; ball or roller screws; gear boxes and other speed changers, including torque converters; flywheels and pulleys, including pulley blocks; clutches and shaft couplings (including universal joints); parts thereof.' The spool valve is a part of transmission control mechanisms and falls within the scope of 'parts thereof' under heading 8483. Subheading 8483.90 covers 'Toothed wheels, chain sprockets and other transmission elements presented separately; parts.' The spool valve, as a metal part of a transmission control assembly, classifies as 'Other' parts under 8483.90.80.00. Section XVI note 2(b) provides that parts suitable for use solely or principally with a particular kind of machine are classified with that machine or in the appropriate parts heading. A transmission spool valve is suitable for use solely with automatic transmissions, supporting classification in heading 8483 as a transmission part.
exclusions_against: Section XVI note 1(g) excludes 'Parts of general use, as defined in note 2 to section XV, of base metal' but a transmission spool valve is not a part of general use—it is specifically designed for transmission control.

The rulings found (N348390, N268111) classify similar valve body assemblies and valve bodies under heading 8481 (Valves), not 8483, which suggests valve components may be more appropriately classified as valves rather than transmission parts.

facts.material: Aluminum alloys (aluminum predominates by weight over each other element)
facts.form: Sheets in cut lengths, various thicknesses exceeding 0.2 mm, not clad, presumed rectangular/square

gri_path: GRI 1: Heading 7606 covers aluminum plates, sheets and strip of a thickness exceeding 0.2 mm; product matches this description exactly
GRI 1: Section XV note 1 exclusions do not apply (not paints, headgear, machinery, vehicles, precious metal, etc.)
GRI 6: Subheading 7606.12 (alloys) vs 7606.11 (not alloyed) - alloy composition confirmed by Chapter 76 Subheading Note 1(b)
GRI 6: 7606.12.30 (Not clad) selected over clad subheadings per facts
GRI 6: Statistical suffix 'Other' (7606.12.30.96) selected absent evidence of specific alloy type (high-strength heat-treatable, heat-treatable industrial, can stock, body/lid stock)

rejected_alternatives.reason: Product is an aluminum alloy, not non-alloyed aluminum, per Chapter 76 Subheading Note 1
No facts indicate specific high-strength heat-treatable, heat-treatable industrial, body stock, or lid stock alloy classification; 'Other' is the residual default absent that information
Those subheadings apply to non-rectangular shapes; product is presumed rectangular/square in cut lengths

missing_facts: Whether sheets are rectangular (including square) or irregular in shape
Specific alloy type (high-strength heat-treatable, heat-treatable industrial, or other per statistical notes 6 and 7)
Exact thickness to confirm it exceeds 0.2 mm as required by the heading text
classification.rationale: Heading 7606 expressly covers aluminum plates, sheets and strip of thickness exceeding 0.2 mm, and the described alloyed, non-clad, cut-length sheets fit this text under GRI 1 with no Section XV exclusion applying. GRI 6 places the goods under 7606.12 (alloys, per Chapter 76 Subheading Note 1(b)) and then 7606.12.30 (not clad); absent specification of a particular heat-treatable alloy type, the residual 'Other' statistical suffix 7606.12.30.96 is the appropriate default, consistent with supporting in-force rulings N301182, N301187, and N333593 on similar aluminum alloy sheet products. Confidence is tempered because shape (rectangular vs. irregular) and specific alloy classification were not confirmed.

7606.argument: Heading 7606 covers aluminum plates, sheets and strip of a thickness exceeding 0.2 mm. The product is alloyed aluminum sheets in cut lengths with thicknesses exceeding 0.2 mm, matching the heading's scope precisely. Chapter 76 Subheading Note 1(b) defines aluminum alloys as metallic substances in which aluminum predominates by weight over each of the other elements, which matches the stated composition. The sheets are not clad (as confirmed by the facts). Under GRI 6, subheading 7606.12 applies to aluminum alloys (as opposed to 7606.11 for non-alloyed aluminum). The 8-digit line 7606.12.30 covers sheets that are not clad. The 10-digit code 7606.12.30.96 (Other) is the appropriate statistical suffix for aluminum alloy sheets not otherwise specified as high-strength heat-treatable alloys, heat-treatable industrial alloys, can stock body or lid stock, or other specifically enumerated categories. Section XV note 1 does not exclude aluminum sheets from chapter 76. The product is not machinery, vehicles, or any other excluded article.

facts.function: Outerwear jacket for upper body coverage
facts.end_use: Worn by men and boys as casual or athletic outerwear

gri_path: GRI 1: Heading 6101 covers men's/boys' overcoats, anoraks, windbreakers and similar articles, knitted or crocheted, other than those of 6103; jackets fall within 'similar articles'
Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms coverage of made-up knitted articles; Note 2 exclusions (6212 goods, worn clothing, orthopedic items) do not apply
GRI 6: subheading 6101.30 for man-made fibers, then 'Other' (not leather/wool content triggers), then statistical suffix for men's vs boys'

rejected_alternatives.reason: Heading 6110 covers sweaters, pullovers, sweatshirts, vests and similar knit tops; a jacket designed as outerwear is more specifically described by 6101's enumerated list of overcoats, anoraks, windbreakers and similar articles

Heading 6103 covers suit-type jackets and blazers meant to be part of a suit/ensemble with matching trousers; description gives no indication this is a suit-coat/blazer rather than a general outerwear jacket, and 6101 expressly excludes goods of 6103 rather than the reverse

missing_facts: Whether the garment is specifically a suit-type jacket/blazer (would push to 6103) versus general outerwear like a windbreaker/anorak (6101) - assumed general outerwear absent contrary indication
Separate statistical treatment needed for boys' units (6101.30.20.20) since description covers both men's and boys' garments
classification.rationale: Heading 6101 specifically enumerates 'overcoats, carcoats, capes, cloaks, anoraks (including ski-jackets), windbreakers and similar articles' knitted or crocheted, which is the most apt description for a generic men's/boys' knit jacket absent facts indicating it is a suit-type jacket or blazer (6103) or a sweater-like garment (6110). Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms coverage and Note 2's exclusions do not apply. Under GRI 6, the polyester (man-made fiber) content places it in 6101.30, and since it does not meet the leather or wool content thresholds it falls to the residual 'Other' 8-digit line, with 6101.30.20.10 as the men's statistical suffix; boys' garments would separately fall under 6101.30.20.20.

6101.argument: Heading 6101 covers men's or boys' overcoats, carcoats, capes, cloaks, anoraks (including ski-jackets), windbreakers and similar articles, knitted or crocheted. The product is a men's and boys' knit jacket made from 100% polyester, which is a made-up knitted garment designed for upper body coverage as outerwear. Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms this chapter applies only to made-up knitted or crocheted articles, which this product satisfies. The product is not excluded by Chapter 61 Note 2 (which excludes only heading 6212 goods, worn articles, and orthopedic appliances). Under GRI 1, heading 6101 is the most specific provision for knitted jackets for men and boys. The subheading 6101.30 applies because the jacket is made of man-made fibers (100% polyester). Within 6101.30, the product falls under 6101.30.20 (Other), and then 6101.30.20.10 for men's jackets (or 6101.30.20.20 for boys' jackets when classified separately). The product does not contain 25% or more leather (6101.30.10) or 23% or more wool (6101.30.15), so 6101.30.20.10 is the correct classification for the men's version.

6110.argument: Heading 6110 covers 'Sweaters, pullovers, sweatshirts, waistcoats (vests) and similar articles, knitted or crocheted.' Men's and boys' knit jackets fall squarely within this heading as 'similar articles' to the enumerated items. Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms this chapter applies only to 'made up knitted or crocheted articles,' which these jackets are. The product is 100% polyester (man-made fiber), placing it in subheading 6110.30 'Of man-made fibers.' Within that subheading, the product does not contain 25% or more leather (6110.30.10), 23% or more wool (6110.30.15), or 30% or more silk (6110.30.20), so it falls under 6110.30.30 'Other.' The 10-digit code 6110.30.30.10 is the appropriate statistical line for men's garments, with 6110.30.30.15 for boys' garments. Since the product covers both men and boys, 6110.30.30.10 (men's) is the primary classification. Ruling F86718 (in force) classified a men's jacket of 95% polyester, 5% polyurethane as 6110.30.3050 (now 6110.30.30.53 under current HTS). Ruling N121122 (in force) classified a men's jacket of 80% cotton, 20% polyester as 6110.20.2079. Both rulings confirm that knit jackets of polyester or polyester-blend construction are properly classified in heading 6110.
exclusions_against: Chapter 61 Note 2(a) excludes goods of heading 6212 (track suits, ski suits, swimwear, etc.), but knit jackets are not track suits or ski suits and are not excluded.
Chapter 61 Note 2(b) excludes worn clothing, but these are new garments.
Chapter 61 Note 2(c) excludes orthopedic appliances and surgical items, which do not apply.

6103.argument: Heading 6103 covers 'Men's or boys' suits, ensembles, suit-type jackets, blazers, trousers, bib and brace overalls, breeches and shorts (other than swimwear), knitted or crocheted.' The product is a men's and boys' knit jacket made from 100% polyester. Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms this chapter applies only to made-up knitted or crocheted articles, which this product is. The jacket is a suit-type jacket or blazer under heading 6103. At the 6-digit level, 6103.43 covers trousers and related items of synthetic fibers, but the heading text explicitly includes 'suit-type jackets' and 'blazers' as primary articles. The 10-digit code 6103.43.15.20 is the most specific provision for men's synthetic fiber jackets under this heading. Two in-force CBP rulings (N283232 and N111600) classify 100% polyester men's knit jackets at 6103.30.2010, confirming that polyester knit jackets for men belong in heading 6103. Chapter 61 Note 2 does not exclude this product. The product meets all requirements: it is made-up, knitted, and designed for men and boys as outerwear.
